newsitem.title: FRANCE: France won't patrol beyond 32nd parallel in Iraq. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: France won't patrol beyond 32nd parallel in Iraq. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]

text.p: France said on Thursday it would continue to take part in allied air patrols of a no-fly zone over southern Iraq but its planes would not cross the 32nd parallel despite the U.S. extension of the zone (corrects by rewording and inserting dropped word 'not').

A foreign ministry statement said the decision had been taken after visiting U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher assued French leaders the U.S. operation "Desert Strike" to punish Baghdad for sending troops into Kurdish areas of northern Iraq was finished.

France once again pointedly refrained from approving President Bill Clinton's two cruise missile raids on Iraq this week or his decision to extend the no-fly zone to the 33rd parallel, just south of Baghdad.

"Under these circumstances, France will continue to participate in the "Provide Comfort" and "Southern Watch" surveillance missions. Concerning "Southern Watch", its participation will take place south of the 32nd parallel," the Foreign Ministry statement said.

Officials said French planes had suspended their reconnaissance flights in the "Provide Comfort" operation over northern Iraq, including the Kurdish battle zone, on Tuesday, date of the first U.S. missile attack, and had kept south of the 30th parallel in southern Iraq.
The new decision would take effect next Monday, the Foreign Ministry said.
